evidence_items.publisher: arXiv; Stephanie Lin, Jacob Hilton, and Owain Evans
evidence_items.explanation: The evaluation includes GPT-3 and supports the narrower observation that language models produce false answers. Its deliberately challenging questions and focus on imitated misconceptions do not establish a general fabrication rate or the absence of a cognitive model as its cause.

The GPT-3-based intervention improved truthfulness but still sometimes relied on unreliable sources. Browsing, training, and answer selection changed together, so this is evidence of partial remediation rather than an isolated test of Marcus's causal explanation.

receipt.public_excerpt: InstructGPT models show improvements in truthfulness over GPT-3.

evidence_items.explanation: Human-feedback training improved truthful answering and reduced unsupported additions on closed-domain tasks, without introducing an explicit external world-model module. These modified models provide counterweight to a strong reading of remediation difficulty, but improvement does not demonstrate a reliable general fix.

unresolved_gaps: No located study independently establishes that GPT-3 lacks the relevant representations and that this absence causes its factual errors.
The remediation studies change several factors or model training, leaving the claimed mechanism unidentified.
The claim supplies no standard for deciding when remediation is sufficiently easy or reliable.
